messages.subject: welcome student contributor to glmmTMB
messages.body_plain:
Dear TMB users,

I’m very happy to announce that we’ll be hosting an undergraduate student collaborator, Divit Purwar, over the summer, via the Google Summer of Code program. Divit will be forking glmmTMB and converting the likelihood code from TMB to RTMB to make it easier for more people to contribute in the future. You will probably see some questions from Divit posted here when it pertains to this group. It would be great if replying to these questions could be a joint community effort and then the questions and answers can benefit other users.

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2026/wiki/glmmTMB-via-RTMB

Cheers,

Mollie

On behalf of Ben and Kasper

messages.subject: as.logical(advector)
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I'm trying to use a combination of differentiable max and as.logical to identify the first index in a vector with a value above 0.

max2 = function(x,y){(x + y + abs(x - y)) / 2}
idx <- sapply(advec , max2 , 0 , simplify = TRUE)
value <- vec[as.logical(idx)][1]

I'm finding that as.logical returns TRUE for all idx, even when the value is 0 (unlike as.logical(0L), which returns FALSE.

I imagine this is expected behavior in RTMB, but has anyone dealt with a similar problem and come up with a solution? For my issue specifically, advec is constantly increasing so idx will be all 0's until the first positive value. I'd prefer not to use use RTMB:::getValues.

Thanks in advance,
Abe

I can use the output of f to isolate the value x[f(x)]. However, if I use the output to try and replace a value x[f(x)] <- AD(0) for example, I get an error "invalid subscript type 'complex'". ADOverload is enabled for  "[<-". I'm having a somewhat difficult time circumventing this. Among others, I've tried c(head(x , f(x)-1) , AD(0) , tail(x , f(x)-1)), x[cumsum(rep(1 , f(x)]...  which also fail.

Thanks again for taking a look.
-Abe

messages.subject: Re: welcome student contributor to glmmTMB
messages.body_plain:
As a shameless plug, I just want to point out that RTMBdist <https://janolefi.github.io/RTMBdist/> exists as a library of non-standard distributions compatible with RTMB.

It would be great if Divit keeps this in mind because
a) I ran into various minor and major hurdles when first implementing custom distributions (which are now overcome for the most part), so using RTMBdist probably saves time, and
b) if the package is used more, stability will be checked by more people and more bugs will be found. I'm happy about any issue opened on Github. :)

Cheers
